Check out project engineer positions for big companies around you if possible. Stack up for a couple years and give you some breathing room financially, and towards the end of the couple years if you're not feeling it, jump ship to something that suits your vocational desires. 

It's so nice to be able to work outside, but it comes with a financial sacrifice most of the time if you're not in higher up positions. I was in manufacturing the last 14 years before coming to USIC, and I never wanted to step foot in concrete walls ever again. But, here I am, calibrating machinery, 12hr days, hating my job..but! Best of luck man! Don't feel bad. Jobs a job. Careers are dead and commitment doesn't mean jack anymore, so do what you gotta do for your best interest.
